messages:
maya: seeing high pod churn in sfo-az3, autoscaler marking ~20 nodes Unhealthy, traffic shift started
santiago: yep, control-plane API latency spiked around 04:12 UTC, etcd leader flaps
oncall-bot: Incident created by maya - SFO AZ3 control-plane instability affecting pod readiness
elaine: reroute to ams + lax triggered, some tail latency increase p99 in ams
ryan: traffic shift worked but cost for dedicated pools spiked during the surge
maya: warm pool didn't seem to kick in — several pools were below expected spare capacity
santiago: confirmed; warm-pool autoscale blocked by failing instance health-probes
devops: quick check - are kubelet logs showing connection or OOM issues?
santiago: grabbing logs now, snippet below:
```
kubectl -n infra logs -l node-role=gpu --since=10m
tail -n 200 /var/log/kubelet.log
```
maya: logs show repeated "connection refused" to etcd leader from nodes in az3
ops-runbooks: added note to runbook draft: verify API server endpoints, etcd members, and instance probe responses before performing traffic shift
elaine: suggestion: require 2 consecutive green health checks (30s apart) before unmuting routes
santiago: +1. also add a pre-shift dry-run that simulates node drain to estimate capacity delta
ryan: action: add cost guardrail that blocks >20% spend spike without leadership approval during emergency shifts
devops: I'll write a helper script to validate GPU driver + kernel modules and restart kubelet if transient failure detected
maya: temporary request-throttling during shift reduced client retries and helped flatten the curve
ops-runbooks: created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/129 - includes SFO control-plane flow, health checks, and pre-shift checklist
maya: playbook snippet we used during the incident:
```
# pre-shift checks
./scripts/check_etcd.sh sfo-az3
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide | grep Unready
```
elaine: can we add a synthetic end-to-end test that validates <250ms 95th before unmuting a route?
santiago: added a CI job to run synthetic traffic; will gate the shift in next deploy window
maya: postmortem item: increase ASG drain grace from 300s -> 600s to let model processes exit cleanly
ryan: also add a "failover-cost-threshold" alert to notify #finance when triggered during incidents
devops: assigning runbook tasks: devops (script + tests), santiago (ci + health-checks), ryan (alerts + finance hook). ETA: EOD tomorrow
ops-runbooks: updated runbook section "Traffic Shift Safety" with explicit checklists, commands, and rollback steps. PR merged
maya: thanks — we'll run a tabletop next week to validate the new flow and timings
oncall-bot: Incident resolved: control-plane stabilized, nodes rejoined sfo-az3, traffic normalized (1806123810)
santiago: closing thread; I'll add timestamps and owners to each runbook step and link the postmortem doc
